highlights.title: SENTINEL-RL: Offloading Topological Reasoning from LLM Agents in the Security Operations Center
highlights.summary: Sentinel‑RL is an SOC agent architecture that separates topological reasoning from language reasoning by encoding live authentication graphs into a fixed‑dimensional state for a PPO policy, letting an LLM generate analyst‑readable narratives based on the policy’s actions.
highlights.detail: The finite context window of LLMs prevents them from holding multi‑thousand‑host graphs, so Sentinel‑RL offloads that to a graph attention encoder. The PPO policy selects from a constrained action set, ensuring topology‑consistent containment steps. An LLM then produces human‑friendly explanations, gated by a critic for safety. The design was evaluated on the LANL Comprehensive dataset.

highlights.title: CORE: Improving Compositional Reasoning in MLLM Embedding via Reranker Distillation
highlights.summary: CORE enhances compositional reasoning in multimodal‑language‑model embeddings by distilling a cross‑attentive reranker's fine‑grained judgments using a Rank‑KL objective trained on five‑level candidate lists.
highlights.detail: CORE generates candidate lists spanning five compositional matching levels and trains the embedding model to mimic the reranker's ranking via a KL‑divergence loss. Experiments compare contrastive learning, CoSENT, and Rank‑KL under identical data and tuning budgets. Results show CoSENT and Rank‑KL exploit the multi‑level supervision better than contrastive, with Rank‑KL achieving the highest overall performance.

highlights.title: IRWOZ 2.0: A Large Language Model-driven Dialogue Dataset for Industrial Robot Conversations
highlights.summary: IRWOZ 2.0 expands the industrial robot dialogue dataset to 390 conversations across four domains and raises GPT‑2’s BLEU‑4 score from 0.1651 to 0.5604.
highlights.detail: The new version uses LLM‑enhanced generation (Mistral/Claude‑3.5) and manual corrections to clean noisy states and utterances. Automated typo removal further improves data quality. Benchmarking shows a substantial boost in dialogue state‑tracking accuracy, making the dataset more reliable for HRI research.

highlights.title: NeoMME: an efficient Multimodal-native and Multilingual Encoder
highlights.summary: NeoMME is presented as an efficient multimodal‑native, multilingual encoder.
highlights.detail: The announcement appears on the Hugging Face blog, indicating the model targets both multimodal inputs and multiple languages while emphasizing computational efficiency. No quantitative metrics or release details are provided in the excerpt.

highlights.title: Porting my 1993 Amiga game to Godot, with an LLM reading the 68000 assembly
highlights.summary: A 1993 Amiga MC68000 game was ported to Godot using Claude Fable 5, achieving a binary identical to the original except for a 108‑byte mismatch.
highlights.detail: The author fed Claude their decades of memory, notes, and repository history; the model assembled the code with vasm on a Mac. Initial draft took an evening, with final polishing over several weekends. The small byte discrepancy highlights subtle differences in assembly pipelines.

items.title: Daybreak for Frontline Defenders: $1B to protect essential services
items.summary: OpenAI announced Daybreak for Frontline Defenders, committing $1 billion to expand access to frontier cyber‑AI tools, training, and support for essential services.
items.detail: Daybreak aims to provide advanced cyber‑security AI capabilities to organizations that protect critical infrastructure. The funding will cover model deployment, user training, and ongoing technical assistance, positioning the initiative as a large‑scale public‑private partnership.

items.title: Introducing WeatherNext 3, our most advanced and accurate global weather AI model
items.summary: DeepMind introduced WeatherNext 3, its most advanced and accurate global weather AI model.
items.detail: WeatherNext 3 builds on previous iterations with improved resolution and forecasting horizons, leveraging larger training datasets and refined neural architectures. The blog post highlights its potential for climate research and operational forecasting, though specific performance numbers are not disclosed.

items.title: Legora reviewed 41 documents in minutes with GPT-6 Astra
items.summary: Legora used GPT‑6 Astra to review 41 financial documents in minutes, detecting all four planted errors and improving workflow performance by roughly 40%.
items.detail: The test involved a financial‑review workflow where GPT‑6 Astra parsed each document, flagged inconsistencies, and suggested corrections. Detecting every planted error demonstrated high reliability, while the speed and accuracy gains translated into a measurable productivity boost for the team.

items.title: Playco cut manual fixes 50% prototyping games with GPT-6 Astra
items.summary: Playco built three themed game prototypes from a single grey‑box using GPT‑6 Astra and saw a 50% reduction in manual fixes compared with the previous model.
items.detail: Starting from a minimal grey‑box foundation, GPT‑6 Astra generated assets, level layouts, and narrative elements for three distinct themes. The reduced need for manual adjustments accelerated development cycles, illustrating the model’s utility for rapid prototyping in game design.

items.title: ZGateway: Learnings from Putting a Proxy in Front of ZippyDB
items.summary: Meta released ZGateway, a proxy for ZippyDB that unifies traffic and adds admission control, load balancing, cross‑region resilience, and richer operations to the key‑value store serving billions of entries.
items.detail: ZGateway sits in front of ZippyDB, Meta’s most widely used key‑value store for product metadata and counters. By centralizing traffic, it enables consistent admission policies and simplifies cross‑region replication, improving overall system robustness and operational visibility.

items.title: Hackaday Europe 2026: Fluid Kernels and Optimizing C++ for MCUs
items.summary: Hackaday Europe 2026 covered fluid kernels and techniques for optimizing C++ code on microcontrollers.
items.detail: The article discusses how fluid kernels can adapt to varying workloads on constrained devices and presents best practices for C++ compilation, memory layout, and power‑aware scheduling to squeeze maximum performance from MCUs.

items.title: Security updates for Thursday
items.summary: Thursday security updates were issued for multiple Linux distributions, including kernel, Firefox, Node.js, and various library packages across AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, Mageia, Oracle, and SUSE.
items.detail: The updates address vulnerabilities in components such as the Linux kernel, freerdp, nodejs versions 22 and 24, and Firefox ESR. Each distro’s package manager provides the patched versions, and administrators are urged to apply them promptly to maintain system security.

items.title: Audacity 4.0 released
items.summary: Audacity 4.0, the new version of the audio editor, introduces a Qt‑based interface, user‑interface “Workspaces”, and a new .aup4 project format.
items.detail: The rewrite moves the UI from wxWidgets to Qt, enabling higher‑DPI scaling and theming. Workspaces let users store multiple panel layouts and switch instantly. The .aup4 format replaces the older XML project files but drops some 3.x features, so migration may require manual adjustments.

items.title: [$] Recent work in memory tiering
items.summary: Tiered‑memory systems combine DRAM with faster high‑bandwidth or slower CXL memory, and allocation placement heavily impacts workload performance.
items.detail: While tiered designs have existed for years, recent research momentum appears to have slowed, with only a handful of new proposals. Current efforts explore optimal placement algorithms and question whether the added complexity justifies the performance gains on heterogeneous memory stacks.

items.title: A Split Keyboard Designed for Human Hands
items.summary: A newly designed split keyboard is ergonomically shaped for human hands, echoing 19th‑century design cues.
items.detail: The keyboard retains the classic staggered key layout but splits the halves to match natural shoulder width, reducing wrist strain. Its construction uses modern materials while preserving the tactile feel of vintage typewriters, appealing to both nostalgia and ergonomics enthusiasts.

items.title: A Thoroughly Modern Minimalist Transceiver
items.summary: A modern minimalist transceiver reuses classic radio architecture with contemporary components to create a compact, safe design.
items.detail: By building on proven schematics, the project avoids the pitfalls of wholly novel designs, allowing rapid prototyping. The minimalist approach reduces part count and power consumption, making it suitable for hobbyist experimentation and low‑cost deployments.

items.title: Barnacle: Adaptive Multi-Leader Scheduling for DAG-Based Consensus
items.summary: Barnacle adds adaptive multi‑leader scheduling to DAG consensus, adjusting leader count at runtime without extra messages.
items.detail: Barnacle measures the fraction of slots decided by the direct rule on the committed DAG each interval and applies additive‑increase, multiplicative‑decrease to tune leader slots. The approach is deterministic and requires no additional cryptographic overhead, and it can be instantiated on multiple existing DAG protocols.

items.title: NACRE: Rethinking Confidential Containers through Native Architectural Support
items.summary: NACRE is a RISC‑V hardware‑software co‑design that enables native confidential containers by separating host authority from protected state access.
items.detail: Container identities are recognized in hardware, routing privileged traps to an isolated S‑mode agent. An M‑mode monitor validates identity, mapping, and page transitions before committing them, preventing a compromised host kernel from reading or modifying protected container memory.

items.title: From Data Querying to Data Investigations: Rethinking Natural Language Interfaces for Databases
items.summary: D² proposes a data‑investigation paradigm for natural‑language database interfaces, using a Murder‑Mystery benchmark to show multi‑step query reasoning.
items.detail: Traditional Text‑to‑SQL assumes a single query, but real users need to explore data through sequences of queries and intermediate results. D² autonomously searches, reasons over, and aggregates data, providing evidence‑backed decisions across multiple SQL steps.

items.title: Lantern: Finding Committable Transactions via Back-Propagation on DAGs
items.summary: Lantern provides deterministic concurrency control for transaction processing by back‑propagating dependency states to commit zero‑out‑degree vertices.
items.detail: All vertices with zero out‑degree in the local dependency graph can be safely committed in ascending order using an overwrite‑permissive strategy. The back‑propagation iteratively updates dependency states from sinks to sources, while CFBS improves throughput for read‑modify‑write intensive workloads.

items.title: Tree Databases
items.summary: The paper defines a tree‑structured database model with labeled directed trees and supports traversal and analytic queries via a functional algebra.
items.detail: Each tree represents an object with attributes encoded as paths from the root. Trees can be combined using defined operations to create new trees, and queries are expressed as functional compositions over these structures, enabling both navigation and aggregation tasks.

items.title: Iapetus: Content-Aware Hierarchical Scheduling for Collaborative ViT Inference in LEO Satellite Networks
items.summary: Iapetus is a content‑aware hierarchical scheduler for collaborative ViT inference on LEO satellites, combining token compression and layer offloading based on quality prediction.
items.detail: The scheduler first screens constellation‑wide options to keep a bounded candidate set, then refines each candidate with predicted quality metrics. It jointly plans token compression levels and layer offloading trajectories, balancing activation transfer costs against satellite contact windows and battery constraints.

items.title: LanRhyme/MicYou
items.summary: MicYou turns an Android device into a high‑quality microphone for a PC, available as an open‑source Rust project.
items.detail: The tool streams audio from the phone to the computer over USB or Wi‑Fi with low latency, providing a cost‑effective alternative to dedicated microphones. Its Rust implementation ensures safety and easy cross‑platform compilation.

items.title: tenstorrent/tt-metal
items.summary: TT‑Metal offers a TT‑NN operator library and low‑level kernel programming model for Tenstorrent hardware, written in C++.
items.detail: TT‑Metal (formerly TT‑Metalium) provides abstractions for building neural‑network operators directly on Tenstorrent chips, exposing fine‑grained control over memory and compute while handling low‑level kernel compilation and execution.

items.title: ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101
items.summary: A GitHub repo that uses visual diagrams and plain language to explain complex system designs, aimed at interview preparation.
items.detail: The repository covers topics such as load balancing, caching, data partitioning, and example architectures. It is organized as markdown files with embedded images, requiring no installation beyond a browser. Engineers can study the material to build intuition for system design interviews.

items.title: CapSoftware/Cap
items.summary: An open‑source Rust project that provides a Loom‑like platform for creating and sharing high‑quality screen recordings.
items.detail: Cap offers customizable recording settings, instant shareable links, and self‑hosting options for privacy. The UI is built with modern web technologies while the core recording engine runs natively in Rust, delivering low‑overhead performance.

items.title: SimoHypers/limusic
items.summary: A native desktop YouTube Music client built with Tauri, Rust, and SvelteKit that provides ad‑free playback via libmpv and integrates Last.fm scrobbling and Discord Rich Presence.
items.detail: By avoiding Electron, the app reduces memory usage and start‑up time. Playback is handled by libmpv, ensuring smooth audio, while built‑in Last.fm scrobbling tracks listening habits and Discord Rich Presence shows the current track on users' profiles. It runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

items.title: addyosmani/agent-skills
items.summary: A collection of production‑grade engineering skill modules designed to enhance AI coding agents' ability to write, test, and refactor code.
items.detail: The repository includes patterns for error handling, code linting, automated test generation, and refactoring suggestions. It integrates with popular LLM APIs, aiming to improve the reliability and maintainability of AI‑generated code in real‑world development pipelines.
